neighbours.label: the descriptive-adjective slot in a physical description of an animal's body (a short, dense coat; strong claws; sharp talons; animals with short legs); animal behaviour without a body description is quiet
fire: The Siberian husky has a thick, double coat that keeps it warm in deep snow.
Moles use their broad front paws to push soil out of the tunnel.
Otters are slender mammals with webbed feet and a long, flat tail.
The heron has a long, pointed bill for spearing frogs and small fish.
Anteaters rip open rotten logs with their powerful curved claws.
The lynx is a medium-sized cat with tufted ears and a short tail.
The Persian has a long, silky coat that needs brushing every day.
Owls grip their prey with strong feet and hooked talons.
quiet: The Siberian husky was bred to pull sleds across deep snow.
Moles spend nearly all of their lives under the ground.
Otters are playful mammals that live near rivers and hunt at night.
The heron stood still for an hour before it flew across the lake.
Anteaters eat thousands of insects every day and sleep in the shade.
The lynx is rarely seen because it hunts alone at night.
The Persian was first shown at a cat show in London in 1871.
Owls hunt at night and rest in hollow trees during the day.

notes: Card: 'has a short, tight coat', 'their strong claws' x3, 'animals with elongated skulls', plus a tea-tasting list ('TASTE:'); the - pole's output promotes ' slightly', ' coarse', ' double', ' rich'. Probes: 'short, dense coat' 0.85, 'strong claws' 0.77, 'sharp talons' 0.63, 'with short legs and' 0.55; a table's 'smooth, dark surface' 0.18, tasting notes 0.18, animal behaviour 0.01-0.08.
